t: By 370 the Huns had reached the Volga; their conquest of the Alans and Goths drove thousands of Goths to seek refuge across the Lower Danube in 376.
Under Attila, sole ruler from 445, the Eastern Roman Empire agreed in 449 to pay an annual tribute of 2,100 pounds of gold; in 451 he invaded Gaul and in 452 Italy.
After Attila died in 453 the Gepid king Ardaric's Germanic coalition defeated his sons at the Battle of Nedao, and the last king Dengizich was killed in Thrace in 469.
dyk: Only three words of the Hunnic language are recorded, all apparently Indo-European; everything else known of it comes from personal and tribal names, so the language is held by many to be unclassifiable.
ev: The Huns arrive on the Volga, setting the Goths and Alans moving westward.
The Huns make their first large-scale attack on the Eastern Roman Empire, overrunning Armenia and pillaging Cappadocia and Thrace, and invade the Sasanian Empire, where they are badly defeated.
The brothers Attila and Bleda force the Eastern Roman Empire to sign the Treaty of Margus, granting the Huns trade rights and an annual tribute.
Attila, sole ruler since Bleda's death in 445, invades the Balkans and Thrace; the war ends in 449 with a tribute of 2,100 pounds of gold a year.
Attila's forces enter Gaul, attack Metz and besiege Orléans; a combined Roman and Visigothic army fights them at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains.
Attila dies of a haemorrhage on his wedding night, having sacked northern Italy the year before and met Pope Leo I near Mantua.
At the Battle of Nedao the Gepid king Ardaric leads a Germanic coalition against Attila's son Ellak; the Huns lose many of their Germanic vassals.
Dengizich is defeated and killed in Thrace; the Huns are absorbed by other peoples such as the Bulgars.

f.capital: No fixed capital: based around the Volga and Don in the 390s and on the Great Hungarian Plain by the 420s
f.predecessor: The Alans and the Greuthungi and Thervingi Goths of the Pontic steppe, whom the Huns conquered; a link to the Xiongnu is debated
f.successor: The Gepid and Amali Gothic kingdoms after the Battle of Nedao; the Bulgars and other Oghur Turkic peoples who absorbed the Huns
